IAM_PERMISSION_DENIED.summary: Caller is not authorised for the requested resource/action.
steps: Confirm the failing principal and resource from the log entry.
Use IAM Policy Troubleshooter or inspect the resource/project IAM policy.
Check whether the required permission belongs to the expected role.
Review recent IAM changes before adding any new binding.
Apply least privilege; do not solve by granting Owner/Editor.

QUOTA_OR_RATE_LIMIT.summary: Requests are being throttled or an account/service quota is exhausted.
steps: Identify the exact quota or rate limit from the error.
Check whether traffic increased or retry behaviour is amplifying load.
Implement exponential backoff with jitter where appropriate.
Reduce unnecessary calls or spread workload.
Request a quota increase only when justified by expected load.

SERVICE_5XX_SPIKE.summary: The service or dependency is returning elevated server errors.
steps: Compare error start time with recent deploy/configuration changes.
Check upstream dependency health and saturation.
Inspect traces/logs for the dominant exception or failing dependency.
Rollback the latest revision if evidence links the regression to release.
Verify recovery using error-rate and latency metrics.

LATENCY_SATURATION.summary: Requests exceed latency objectives and show signs of saturation.
steps: Check p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU, memory and request concurrency.
Separate application latency from downstream dependency latency.
Inspect autoscaling and concurrency settings.
Profile the hot path before only increasing resources.
Validate recovery against the latency SLO.

OOM_KILLED.summary: A container exceeded available memory and was killed.
steps: Confirm OOMKilled/exit 137 and the configured memory limit.
Inspect memory trend, request size and recent code/dependency changes.
Check for leaks or unbounded in-memory queues/caches.
Right-size memory only after understanding expected working set.
Load test the repaired revision.

GKE_CRASHLOOP.summary: A Kubernetes workload repeatedly fails to start or remain healthy.
steps: kubectl describe the Pod and inspect events.
kubectl logs the current and previous container instance.
Check image, command, environment, ConfigMaps, Secrets and mounted resources.
Check startup/readiness/liveness probes.
Rollback or fix configuration, then verify restart count stabilises.

PUBSUB_BACKLOG.summary: Subscribers are not processing messages at the arrival rate.
steps: Inspect backlog and oldest-unacked-message age.
Check subscriber errors, latency and ack deadline behaviour.
Look for poison messages or repeated redelivery.
Check subscriber concurrency/autoscaling and downstream bottlenecks.
Scale or optimise only after locating the bottleneck.
Inspect active connections and configured pool sizes.
Check for leaked connections and transaction duration.
Compare service scale-out with database connection capacity.
Bound application pools per instance.
Change database max connections only with capacity justification.

DNS_RESOLUTION_FAILURE.summary: The workload cannot resolve a required hostname.
steps: Confirm exact hostname and resolver error.
Check DNS record/zone and recent DNS/network changes.
Validate private-zone visibility and VPC/network context.
Test resolution from the affected runtime environment.
Restore the record/path and confirm application recovery.

UNKNOWN.summary: The classifier does not have enough confidence to map this event to a known incident.
steps: Escalate for human triage.
Search surrounding logs/traces/metrics.
If a recurring incident pattern is confirmed, add a runbook and retraining examples.
